images.title: Three pieces each, different sizes
images.purpose: Show two parathas of exactly the same size, one cut into 4 equal pieces and one into 10, with 3 pieces taken from each, so the child sees that the 1/4 pieces are bigger than the 1/10 pieces.
images.composition: Two round parathas side by side at the same height, the name above each, its fraction and number of pieces below, and the comparison written large at the bottom.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. Two flat round parathas of exactly the same size, each a circle 320 px across (radius 160) with a thin dark #2B2B2B outline (3 px), their centres on one level at y 340 and at x 400 (left) and x 1056 (right). Every cut line is a thin dark straight line (2 px) from the centre to the edge, counted from the top (12 o'clock) going clockwise. LEFT PARATHA: cut by exactly 4 lines, at 12, 3, 6 and 9 o'clock, into exactly 4 equal pieces of 90 degrees each; 3 pieces are filled teal #0072B2 (the pieces from 12 o'clock clockwise round to 9 o'clock) and the 1 piece at the top left is white. RIGHT PARATHA: cut by exactly 10 lines into exactly 10 equal pieces of 36 degrees each, the first line at 12 o'clock; the first 3 pieces from 12 o'clock clockwise are filled amber #E69F00 and the other 7 pieces are white. Above the left paratha the name Radhika and above the right paratha the name Raman (40 px, bold, dark #1F2937, about y 110). Under each paratha, about y 575, its fraction in dark bold numerals (72 px): 3/4 under the left and 3/10 under the right; under each fraction, about y 640, a caption in dark (34 px): 4 pieces under the left and 10 pieces under the right. Across the bottom centre, about y 740, one line of bold dark text, 3/4 > 3/10 (80 px), the largest text in the frame. In all 14 pieces, of which 6 are shaded (3 teal, 3 amber). Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
parathas of different diameters, or pieces of unequal size within one paratha
any piece shaded other than the 3 stated on each paratha
images.takeaway: Both take 3 pieces, but a 1/4 piece is bigger than a 1/10 piece, so 3/4 > 3/10.
images.description: Two parathas of the same size, one cut into 4 equal pieces and one into 10, with 3 pieces shaded on each, and 3/4 > 3/10 written below.
images.context: Concept image for Same Number of Pieces, Different Sizes (comparing with the same numerator). It follows the idea of the figure in your maths book (two wholes of the same size cut into different numbers of equal pieces) and shows the concept's own example, 3/4 and 3/10 of two parathas of the same size.
images.teaching_notes: Count the shaded pieces on both (3 and 3) so counting cannot decide, then compare one piece of each: the 1/10 piece is much smaller. The slip to watch is that the bigger bottom number means the bigger fraction.

image_decisions.why: The two same-size parathas cut into 4 and 10 equal pieces make the size of one piece visible, which is what decides the comparison.
